basis: Acute loss of respiratory function defines the condition; cardiovascular shock is a possible complication, not a defining organ lesion.
Congenital sensorineural hearing loss and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; both occur in 80-99%.
Mandibulofacial and limb dysostosis define disease; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Ear shape changes do not establish hearing damage; hearing loss is under 30%.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in skin.
Pheochromocytoma arises in adrenal medullary endocrine tissue; associated hypertension does not establish direct cardiovascular damage.
Hereditary gastric carcinoma arises in the stomach; additional cancers and lymphoma are subtype-specific rather than shared across this umbrella.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy directly affects brain development and function.
Defined by disease of the parasympathetic component of the autonomic nervous system.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are universal in assessed patients; hypotonia is neurologic. Minor digit anomalies do not establish locomotor dysfunction.
Premature ovarian failure entails loss of gonadal endocrine function.
Structural skeletal and extraocular muscle myopathy with defining ophthalmoplegia; respiratory muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Apocrine adenosis is confined to breast tissue, which has no axis.
Substance dependence has no axis; smoking-related organ diseases are separate conditions.
Congenital structural malformation of the anus or rectum; urinary tract involvement is subtype-specific.
Viral infection causes acute liver failure; hepatic encephalopathy is required by the definition and establishes neurologic dysfunction.
Germ cell tumour arising in the testis; reproductive tumour origin does not establish gonadal endocrine disease.
Congenital enlargement of the tongue affects an oral structure; endocrine and hepatic findings occur in only 1-4%.
Seminoma arising in testicular germ cells; the reproductive site has no axis.
Recurrent cranial nerve paresis is a neuropathic disorder; ophthalmoplegia reflects nerve dysfunction. Diabetes has no established frequency and is a separate disease.
Umbrella of inborn glycolytic metabolic disorders; blood, muscle and nerve injury differ across subtypes and are not established across most patients.
Malignant bone tumour with chondroblastic differentiation.
Brachydactyly and cerebellar ataxia define the syndrome; nystagmus can reflect cerebellar dysfunction without intrinsic ocular damage.
Carcinoma arising in the thyroid endocrine gland; no common direct injury to another axis is established.
Lysosomal metabolic disease with defining skeletal dysplasia; neurologic and visceral damage varies across subtypes, with no additional organ established across most patients.
Structural disease of intracranial arterial walls; stroke is a separate disease, and listed neurologic symptoms do not establish common direct brain injury.
